stories.summary: A new pancreatic cancer vaccine has successfully sparked immune responses in a vast majority of patients. This development marks a promising step forward in medical research.

stories.summary: China is exporting record amounts of clean energy technology, which is helping reduce global emissions. The surge in renewable equipment exports follows rising international interest in green energy.

stories.summary: Engineers built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that respond to light. The breakthrough could lead to self-healing biological robots that explore fragile aquatic environments.
stories.title: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells

stories.summary: A study found that people with Parkinson's disease who exercised regularly experienced slower declines in memory and movement. Those who exercised over eight hours a week showed almost no cognitive decline.
stories.title: Scientists discover a surprising double benefit of exercise for Parkinson’s

stories.summary: Advocates suggest using low-carbon concrete to reduce emissions during the construction phase of data centres. This approach aims to lower environmental impact before facilities even become operational.
stories.title: Low-carbon concrete could lower emissions before data centres even go online

stories.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs' newly formed fourth line is making a major impact on the ice. The players have helped set the tone and contribute key offensive plays.
stories.title: ‘Fast, predictable, hard hockey’: Maple Leafs’ fourth line making big impact

stories.summary: Troy Stecher scored a late goal to secure a 5-4 victory for the Toronto Maple Leafs. The win marks the team's third consecutive triumph in a competitive matchup.
stories.title: Troy Stecher scores late in regulation to power Maple Leafs past Rangers 5-4

stories.summary: Scientists discovered a sophisticated communication system inside a tiny brain region previously thought to broadcast uniform signals. The targeted messaging helps control learning, attention, and behavior.
stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden messaging system deep inside the brain

stories.summary: Conservationists are utilizing innovative science and community-focused programs to protect snow leopards and their habitats. These initiatives aim to foster peaceful coexistence between local herders and the wild cats.
stories.title: World Snow Leopard Day: Community action and new science foster coexistence with humans

stories.summary: Toronto youth under 18 voted to select the city's very first tree of the year. Young residents chose from five native tree species in a special municipal poll.
stories.title: Toronto kids voted for the city's first 'tree of the year.' This is their sweet choice

stories.summary: Cambridge researchers developed a $10 optical sensor that brings laboratory precision to wearable technology. The device accurately identified substances in tests and can monitor health markers like blood glucose non-invasively.
stories.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist

stories.summary: Researchers have identified a specialized immune defense that targets aggressive small cell lung cancer. These immune cells can destroy cancer cells even when the tumors attempt to disguise themselves.
stories.title: Scientists discover a hidden immune weapon against deadly lung cancer

stories.summary: Physicists solved a decades-old quantum physics problem known as the Kondo effect. The scientific breakthrough resolves long-standing questions regarding particle interactions and quantum behavior.
stories.title: Scientists Just Cracked a Quantum Mystery That's Puzzled Physicists For Decades

stories.summary: A recent study shows that specially designed buoys and kites can effectively deter seabirds from approaching fishing nets. These visual tools help protect vulnerable bird species from accidental entanglement.
stories.title: Googly-eyed buoys and kites help keep seabirds out of fishing nets, study finds

stories.summary: NASA highlighted a view of the Andromeda galaxy during southern spring in its Astronomy Picture of the Day. The feature includes scientific commentary from a professional astronomer alongside the cosmic image.
stories.title: APOD: 2026 October 23 – Andromeda in Southern Spring

stories.summary: X-ray analysis of soil around Chornobyl revealed that radioactive particles have remained remarkably stable. Rather than releasing harmful fallout into the environment, the particles have locked radiation inside.
stories.title: 40 years later, Chernobyl's nuclear fallout is not what scientists expected

stories.summary: A study of 2,884 exploding stars indicates that dark energy accelerating universe expansion may vary over time. The astronomical discovery challenges fundamental theories in modern cosmology.
stories.title: Nearly 3,000 exploding stars challenge our understanding of the Universe

stories.summary: Researchers found that a daily habit may help delay the aging process in ovaries. Scientists are also testing a drug that could replicate these protective reproductive health benefits.
stories.title: One Habit May Delay Ovarian Aging – And a Drug Could Mimic Its Effects

stories.summary: A 29-foot bronze statue of ancient Persian king Cyrus the Great was installed in Atlanta's Pardis Park. The monument celebrates an enduring historical figure of tolerance and inclusion.
stories.title: A Towering Figure of Tolerance From 2,500 Years Ago Has Found a New Home in Atlanta

stories.summary: The annual Onkel Hans Food Drive successfully collected donations to provide over 37,000 meals to people in need. The food and funds raised will support the Food Bank of Waterloo Region.
stories.title: More than 37K meals provided through Onkel Hans Food Drive

stories.summary: Researchers are exploring new methods to monitor breast cancer that could reduce the need for imaging tests like mammograms. The new approaches aim to help track tumours during chemotherapy and after surgery.
stories.title: Researchers exploring new ways to monitor breast cancer, reducing demand for imaging tests

stories.summary: The westbound lane of the Speedvale bridge in Guelph has reopened ahead of schedule. Traffic will be maintained in the lane until full bridge replacement begins in the spring.
stories.title: Speedvale bridge’s westbound lane reopens early

stories.summary: McMaster University highlighted staff member Benjamin Lebi as part of its community profile series. After moving from Nigeria to Hamilton in 2024, Lebi expressed his joy in joining the university community.
stories.title: Benjamin Lebi finds a home at Mac

stories.summary: Indonesian authorities have paused a massive deforestation project after achieving rice self-sufficiency ahead of schedule. Approximately 4 million acres of rainforest, swamps, and peatlands will be spared from destruction.
stories.title: ‘World’s Largest Deforestation Project’ Halted Early, Saving Potentially 4 Million Acres

stories.summary: The Terry Fox Foundation has received a $25 million donation, which is its largest gift ever. The funds will support a national network connecting cancer centres.
stories.title: Terry Fox never wanted the spotlight. His foundation just received $25 million — its largest gift ever

stories.summary: A clinical trial found that a 15-minute ultrasound-guided procedure provides lasting relief for carpal tunnel syndrome without surgery. The simple fluid treatment freed compressed wrist nerves and significantly reduced pain and numbness in patients.
stories.title: A simple 15-minute treatment could help patients avoid carpal tunnel surgery

stories.summary: A major supermarket group is testing the commercialization of heritage and heirloom apple varieties at scale. The project aims to bring a wider variety of traditional produce options to consumers.
stories.title: Major Supermarket Begins Wide-Scale Tests to Bring Heritage Apple Varieties to Market

stories.summary: A young soccer player from Pickering has earned an invitation to play in Spain with the Barcelona Training Academy. Her dedication and talent have led to international recognition.
stories.title: From Pickering to Spain: rising Ontario soccer star goes global

stories.summary: Japanese chemists conducted experiments demonstrating that coconut oil could be used to create sustainable aviation fuel. The research suggests a new potential application for coconut oil in powering passenger aircraft in the future.
stories.title: Coconut Oil Could Make Great Sustainable Jet Fuel, Pioneering Experiments Demonstrate

stories.summary: Researchers are using advanced breeding techniques to help protect the Cavendish banana from disease and climate threats. The breakthrough offers a potential way to safeguard one of the world's most widely consumed fruits.
stories.title: Have scientists finally found a way to save the banana from disaster?

stories.summary: A new CAR T cell therapy from Kyverna Therapeutics shows promise as a treatment for stiff person syndrome. If approved by the FDA, it would become the first designated treatment for the rare autoimmune disease.
stories.title: This ‘living drug’ could change the course of autoimmune disease

stories.summary: Oxford scientists observed virus-like particles assembling themselves through a process of trial and error. This insight into molecular assembly could aid in developing new vaccines and methods to disrupt viral spread.
stories.title: Oxford scientists discover how viruses build themselves without a blueprint

stories.summary: Researchers developed a powerful laser microscope that enhances image clarity when observing microscopic cellular structures. The technology enables scientists to examine small proteins and better understand interactions between molecular machines in cells.
stories.title: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life

stories.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover captured a vivid new image of wind-carved cliff formations on Mars. Scientists anticipate that these unique geological features may offer clues about ancient volcanic activity on the planet.
stories.title: NASA’s Curiosity rover reveals a spectacular new view of Mars with a mystery on the horizon

stories.summary: Scientists found that a natural plant compound reduced joint swelling and cartilage damage in rats with rheumatoid arthritis. The discovery reveals a potential path to treat the underlying causes of chronic inflammation.
stories.title: Natural compound could fight rheumatoid arthritis at its source

stories.summary: Samoa's Nu’utele Island is showing remarkable ecological recovery just one year after invasive species were removed. Native forests and wildlife are thriving once again in this protected biodiversity area.
stories.title: Samoan Island Witnesses Explosion of Native Wildlife Following Removal of Invasive Rats and Pigs

stories.summary: A new role in local schools focuses on helping Black students feel affirmed, supported, and safe. The initiative aims to foster greater educational success and inclusion.
stories.title: Meet the woman helping foster success for Black students

stories.summary: Two women from Austria and Switzerland have been freed in Niger after more than a year and a half in captivity. Local media and officials confirmed their release.
stories.title: An Austrian and a Swiss woman freed in Niger after a year and half in captivity

stories.summary: Guelph is accepting applications to start new community gardens throughout the area. Residents can apply to establish local growing spaces.
stories.title: Applications now open for new community gardens around Guelph

stories.summary: The University of Guelph proposed a new law school focused heavily on experiential learning. Organizers hope to open the innovative program by 2028.
stories.title: Proposed U of G law school would be 'most innovative in the country'

stories.summary: Saskatchewan is introducing a rapid HIV testing program for mothers giving birth. The initiative helps determine the best care for newborns based on viral loads.
stories.title: Regina mom hopes new HIV testing program will help others giving birth

stories.summary: The New York Public Library received a collection of over 250 prints by artist Kiki Smith. The works will be made accessible to anyone with a library card.
stories.title: New York Public Library Gets Over 250 Kiki Smith Prints, a Gift from the Artist’s Sister Seton Smith

stories.summary: A cocoa farmer in Ghana is demonstrating how forest protection can support local livelihoods. Her work helps build resilience against a changing climate.
stories.title: The farmer growing a future under Ghana’s trees

stories.summary: This historical milestone marks the anniversary of the Soviet Union's Venera 9 mission. It was the first spacecraft to enter orbit around Venus and return surface images.
stories.title: Good News in History, October 22

stories.summary: A newly analyzed fossil provides evidence that a human ancestor appeared much earlier than previously thought. The discovery offers a significant transformation of current evolutionary timelines.
stories.title: New Fossil Confirms a Human Ancestor Appeared 200,000 Years Earlier Than Expected

stories.summary: Researchers have successfully reversed Parkinson's symptoms in mice using a specific low-oxygen drug combination. The treatment demonstrated improvements in movement control during tests.
stories.title: 'Low-Oxygen' Drug Combination Reverses Parkinson's Symptoms in Mice

stories.summary: Airbnb has updated its policies to restrict the extensive cleaning chores hosts can require of guests. Travelers will soon face fewer required tasks before completing their checkout.
stories.title: Airbnb limiting the checkout chores hosts can ask guests to do

stories.summary: An American man has been freed after spending more than four years in a Russian prison. His family reported that he is in disbelief following his release.
stories.title: Sister of American Stephen Hubbard says he’s in disbelief following release by Russia

stories.summary: Doctors have confirmed that Pope Leo XIV requires no further treatment for his lung cancer. Follow-up tests showed that the disease is successfully localized.
stories.title: Pope Leo’s doctors say tests show he needs no further treatment for lung cancer

stories.summary: A social media campaign is helping an elderly man fulfill his decades-long dream of completing a custom boat project. Strangers have rallied together to offer support and kindness to make the project a reality.
stories.title: TikTok Star Is Rallying Strangers to Make an 86-year-old’s Dream Come True (WATCH)
